review: finite independent read-only persisted-security source review

payload.model_provenance: Model/effort specified by dispatch and approved scope; no separate runtime model-attestation tool used.
payload.source_context: Only approved source-excerpts.txt, scope.json and request.txt. scope.json approval-pending text is historical; dispatch reports human approval. No earlier findings or unrelated source read.

assessment: Concrete defects exist in supplied feature/store compositions; production reachability and current-source joins remain root work. Confidentiality and ownership findings are conditional where required downstream code/configuration is absent. This does not certify any package or deployed service.

findings.title: Concurrent code exchange can mint two grants from one authorization code
findings.severity: high / P1 if this helper is exposed with the supplied D1 store
findings.status: confirmed source-level feature/store defect; endpoint reachability unverified
findings.minimal_witness: Start two exchangeCode calls with the same live code, matching client/redirect and valid verifier. Both findAuthCodeByHash reads see consumed_at=null. The first conditional UPDATE consumes it; the second UPDATE affects zero rows but consumeAuthCode returns void and never checks the result. Both proceed to issueMcpGrant and persist distinct grants.
findings.enforcement_gap: Single-use success must be decided at the storage consume operation; read-before-consume and a conditional UPDATE whose outcome is discarded do not enforce it.
findings.counterevidence: Sequential reuse is rejected, expiry/client/redirect/PKCE checks exist, and the token/code hashes are unique. Those controls do not reject the losing concurrent consumer. The D1 header explicitly acknowledges the missing multi-step fence (17-24).
findings.root_verification_needed: Join exchangeCode to actual token-route consumers and their store/wrappers; verify concurrent exchange with a barrier before consume, asserting one grant at most. Do not claim a deployed OAuth exploit without this join.

findings.title: Recovery token check and password/revocation cascade are not one atomic recovery
findings.severity: high / P1 if recovery uses this D1 composition
findings.status: confirmed source-level feature/store defect; endpoint reachability unverified
findings.minimal_witness: A and B both read the same unused recovery token and choose different valid passwords. A completes password write, consumption and revocations. B, paused during hashing after its earlier read, then writes its password and succeeds despite A having already consumed/revoked the token. Separately, failure after the password UPDATE and before revocations leaves a changed password and live prior credentials.
findings.enforcement_gap: Password mutation precedes token consumption; all effects are independent committed statements. Even changing order alone would retain the unchecked losing-consume problem.
findings.counterevidence: Purpose/expiry/consumed checks reject invalid or sequentially reused tokens; a fully completed, uncontended recovery revokes all sessions/grants existing at those statements. Failure is not falsely reported as success. The missing fence is explicitly declared in D1 lines 17-24, so this is an implemented limitation rather than a hidden production-readiness promise.
findings.root_verification_needed: Confirm recovery route/store wiring and any external operation-level serialization. Test the two-reader interleaving and injected failure before credential revocation. Determine the intended atomic recovery contract before repair.

findings.title: Concurrent last-owner mutations can leave a team with no active owner
findings.severity: high / P1 if team management uses this D1 composition
findings.status: confirmed source-level feature/store defect; endpoint reachability unverified
findings.minimal_witness: With exactly active owners A and B, concurrent demotions/removals targeting different owners both read two active owners and pass. Their independent UPDATEs then remove/demote both. The UNIQUE(team_id,user_id) constraint is unaffected and cannot enforce an aggregate last-owner invariant.
findings.counterevidence: Sequential removal/demotion of the sole owner is rejected; initiators and targets are checked for active membership and owner privilege. These are effective sequential controls, not an atomic aggregate guard.
findings.root_verification_needed: Locate actual system-tool/HTTP callers and check whether their whole feature operation is fenced or serialized. Exercise mixed remove/demote as well as two demotions. The supplied D1 binding itself has no such fence.

findings.title: Pre-session token deletion does not enforce concurrent single use
findings.severity: medium / P2; higher consequences depend on login caller
findings.status: confirmed source-level helper/store defect; login consumer absent
findings.minimal_witness: Two consumePreSessionToken calls read the same unexpired row before either DELETE. Both DELETEs resolve (one affects zero rows), and both return true from the previously read expiry.
findings.counterevidence: Later sequential reuse fails because the row is gone. This defect does not by itself expose a session or bypass password checking.
findings.root_verification_needed: Join the actual login POST. Also verify browser binding/origin enforcement: the helper accepts only a bearer token and no browser-specific binding. Its comments rely on same-origin secrecy, but an attacker can obtain an anonymous token in their own browser. If the route accepts that token in a victim's forged login POST without an independent origin/browser binding, the intended login-CSRF defense fails even on its first use. That route-level issue is conditional, not proven by these excerpts.

findings.title: The HTTP credential liveness check is before invocation, not at its eventual commit
findings.severity: high / P1 if the stated mid-flight revocation guarantee is required
findings.status: confirmed enforcement-point mismatch; complete canonical path missing
findings.minimal_witness: Allow assertCredentialLive at HTTP line 289 to succeed, then pause execution inside invokeMutation. Revoke the session, then resume execution/commit. The visible check has already completed; the visible state commit revalidates by/guards and a state revision, but the shown session UPDATE never changes that revision. Without an omitted credential-aware commit check, the operation commits after revocation despite the HTTP comment.
findings.counterevidence: Current credentials are checked at identity resolution and again immediately before invoking the mutation; this does block revocation completed before that second read. Membership revalidation exists, and the design permits some already-admitted membership operations to finish (DESIGN 291, 549). A stronger credential boundary must not be inferred merely from the membership rule. assertAuthorityLive explicitly leaves an already-fenced race open at lines 78-80.
findings.root_verification_needed: Inspect invokeMutationCanonical, admission/revalidateCommitForFence, executor guards, and actual identity/state DB join. Decide which credential revocation boundary is accepted versus proposed; prove its exact enforcement point with controlled revoke-after-invoker-entry timing. Do not equate a helper named commit-time with an atomic commit check.

findings.title: Generated CRUD and first-success producer return full stored rows without projection
findings.severity: high / P1 if passed through to caller
findings.status: confirmed raw producer result; external disclosure conditional on omitted canonical wrapper
findings.minimal_witness: An authorized generated create/update changes a model row that also contains a field the caller cannot read (or a random_secret initializer). generatedCrudExecute returns first.row, and invoke's first committed success returns effects.result unchanged and saves it in the receipt. A pass-through canonical wrapper would serialize the hidden field on the first HTTP success even if viewer reads/replays are correctly projected.
findings.counterevidence: invoke.ts lines 1-9 openly describe an S3 unprojected result stage; it is inappropriate to present that helper as a full S4 API. Runtime invokeMutationCanonical is called by assembly but its body is absent, so it could add projection. Returning/persisting raw server-side state internally is not itself external disclosure. Replay handling is outside the excerpt.
findings.root_verification_needed: Trace generatedCrudExecute through invokeMutationCanonical to the serializer and inspect result projection at first success. Test unreadable ordinary fields and random_secret values independently. Inspect replay separately under changed read grants; storing a raw receipt is insufficient evidence of a replay leak.

findings.title: Public read-policy transcription discards secret metadata and grants every declared field name
findings.severity: high / P1 if canonical model fields include secrets and the projector uses this table
findings.status: confirmed metadata loss; secret disclosure requires omitted model/projector join
findings.minimal_witness: Load a canonical model whose fields map includes ordinary field label and secret field token, with a supported public read mark. canonicalModelFields supplies both names; publicInput constructs secretFields=[] and a public grant over both. If projectRow relies on these secret paths or does not independently identify the stored plain string secret, the public query returns token.
findings.counterevidence: Absent read policy yields zero grants, ruled models are omitted/refused, and the engine projects rows before filtering. The actual mapReadRulesToPolicy acceptance branch after line 875, buildPolicyTable, projectRow/isSecretValue, canonical secret representation, and serve invocation are absent. Runtime may reject unsupported shapes or perform independent redaction. Do not claim a tested public leak from metadata loss alone.
findings.root_verification_needed: Use an actually emitted supported public model with a secret initializer, verify loaded field/type metadata and final response, and inspect field-selector transcription too. Preserve the declared T17/B7 host scope rather than assume every design policy is implemented.

findings.title: Production cookie-authenticated grant route mints credentials without its own CSRF/origin check
findings.severity: medium / P2 for consent/CSRF enforcement gap; token theft not established
findings.status: confirmed route-level missing enforcement; attackability depends on browser/origin deployment
findings.minimal_witness: A POST carrying a valid session cookie, a JSON-parsable body and any nonblank client_id reaches issueMcpGrant without a CSRF token or Origin validation. req.json() does not require an application/json Content-Type. The shown main path dispatches this route directly after a binding gate.
findings.counterevidence: SameSite=Lax normally suppresses session cookies on cross-site POSTs, and same-origin response restrictions normally prevent reading the returned token. Therefore the excerpts do not establish generic cross-site bearer exfiltration. Same-site untrusted origins or broader cookie configuration could still make unauthorized issuance possible. Membership is checked before minting.
findings.root_verification_needed: Inspect trusted-origin policy, any edge middleware, actual cookie Domain/SameSite use, and endpoint consent contract. Check no-token/mismatched-token POST behavior at the actual route. Resolve another conditional contract gap: route comments require a verified actor, but its condition at 164-169 never checks actor.email_verified and resolveIdentity returns that flag without requiring true; determine whether active unverified memberships are reachable.

unresolved_security_joins.evidence: Storage load/query selects by model/id or model, inserts owner as an empty string, and supplied assembly closes over an injected store. Query membership uses context.teamId but the scanned rows have no shown team/owner restriction. Owner authority deliberately skips viewer grants. This is safe only if an upstream trusted selection or model boundary establishes the correct store/record scope.
unresolved_security_joins.minimal_conditional_witness: If two independently scoped teams share the injected record namespace and the same qualified model, membership in T2 plus a member grant can see T1 rows because the shown scan does not correlate those rows to T2. A public grant does not itself remove the design's record/team boundary. Conversely, a verified one-owner store could make the unscoped SQL correct.
unresolved_security_joins.root_verification_needed: Inspect env-assembly production constructor, binding provisioning, artifact app mapping, owner routing/admission, store identity, and records from two teams/owners. Establish whether state and identity truly share the same physical DB and fence. Do not prescribe database topology or mark cross-tenant exposure without this evidence.

unresolved_security_joins.evidence: Raw receipt outcome is visible at invoke.ts 328-338; receipt lookup, receiptIdentityFor implementation, replay consumer and current-access projector are not supplied. No conclusion about completed replay secrecy, app/team/principal receipt isolation or deterministic root routing is justified.
unresolved_security_joins.root_verification_needed: Trace receipt identity fields and current-access replay projection; test same operation ID across two principals/teams and loss of read access before replay.

unresolved_security_joins.evidence: Completed sign-out-everywhere/recovery revoke sessions and grants but not outstanding authorization codes. A still-valid unconsumed preexisting code plus its verifier can later mint a fresh grant, without session revalidation in exchangeCode. This is a sequential behavior, not only a race.
unresolved_security_joins.root_verification_needed: Determine whether the accepted recovery/global-revocation contract invalidates outstanding authorization authority as well as already-issued grants. Check consent/issuance provenance and token-route reachability. Do not silently expand revocation policy.

unresolved_security_joins.evidence: The supplied engine reads a starting revision, membership and rows; the wrapper after engine.ts 815 is missing, so absence of a final read-fence check cannot be inferred. Invitation accept/revoke storage methods are present but invitation feature/route consumers are absent; no addressed-email, role-ceiling or acceptance-race verdict is possible.
unresolved_security_joins.root_verification_needed: Inspect final query/invokeRead wrappers and invitation callers before claiming violations of DESIGN 291 or 558.

positive_evidence: resolveIdentity checks current token hash records for revocation and expiry on each call; team-bound MCP grants reject explicit team mismatch and missing active membership (context.ts 117-152).
Sessions distinguish authentication from active membership; an actor with null membership is not itself a bypass. Subsequent operation policy must decide access.
OAuth authorization checks registered redirect exact match and PKCE; exchange validates client, redirect, expiry, consumption and S256 verifier before minting (oauth.ts 139-153, 229-245).

Viewer engine resolves grant predicates, projects each matching row before caller filters and sorting, and returns no rows for zero grants (engine.ts 714-788). Secret projection internals are outside the payload.

State mutations use a revision fence and revalidation; the presence of those mechanisms is evidence against blanket claims that state commits have no concurrency control (invoke.ts 299-350; state/storage/d1.ts 670-698). Their coverage of identity writers is a separate issue.
Raw credential material is returned at issuance while only hashes are persisted in the shown identity store. No logging of those raw issuance values appears in the selected route.
limits: Only frozen selected ranges were reviewed. Full source files, tests, deployed configuration, earlier assessments and current changes were not accessed.
No product source edits, network calls, tests, deployments, model launches or subagents were performed. Only the authorized private report was written.
Witnesses are reasoned interleavings/inputs, not executed reproductions. High severity for conditional paths describes impact if root confirms reachability and contract.

Comments describing desired joins do not establish implemented joins; comments explicitly admitting interim limitations were preserved as counterevidence. Helpers alone do not establish endpoint exposure.

Root must join each source path/hash/range to current code, inspect named missing callers/configuration, independently adjudicate and route any narrowly scoped repairs. No new topology, security/resource policy or package acceptance is selected here.
